text: You want to give an AI agent one job. Research a market. Prepare a launch. Move the business forward.
But before the work begins, you're choosing models, connecting company knowledge, adding skills, shaping behavior, wiring services, and setting up payments.
The brief lives in one place. The documents live somewhere else. Every new agent asks for context you have already given.
More agents mean more handoffs. Different instructions. Missing sources. Conflicting answers. You become the coordinator.
And now, agents can spend. Which service was paid? What did inference cost? Who approved it? A useful answer is only part of the job.
The result? More setup. More copying. More supervision. Less time doing the work that matters.
Businesses need agents that share the right context, have clear responsibilities, and work within visible limits.
Because the goal is not to manage more AI tools. It's to get real work done.
